questions.q: The term "sustainable development" was first mentioned in a book related to the 1972 UN Stockholm conference on ____.
questions.explanation: The 1972 UN Conference on the Human Environment in Stockholm produced early literature in which the term 'sustainable development' first appeared.

questions.q: Environmental sustainability focuses on impacts of processes, products and services on ____.
questions.explanation: Environmental sustainability looks at all ecological impacts, including those on water, biodiversity and human health, so every option applies.

questions.q: Which of the following does not come under social sustainability?
questions.explanation: Revenue generation is an economic concern. Labour practices, human rights and business ethics are social sustainability issues.

questions.q: SDG ____ focuses on clean water and sanitation.
questions.explanation: SDG 6 is Clean Water and Sanitation. SDG 1 is No Poverty, SDG 3 is Good Health and Well-being, and SDG 17 is Partnerships for the Goals.
SDG 16 is Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions. The other options are SDGs 1, 2 and 3.

questions.q: On 20 October 2020, the Higher Education Sustainability Initiative (HESI) raised the flag of higher education as a driver for sustainable development and inclusive societies on the first day of the ____ 2020.
questions.explanation: HESI used the opening day of UNESCO's Global Education Meeting 2020 to promote higher education as a driver of sustainable development and inclusive societies.

questions.q: Education is related to all SDGs.
questions.explanation: Education is a goal in its own right (SDG 4), and it also builds the knowledge, skills and values needed to reach every other SDG.

questions.q: Successful implementation of ESD requires a shift in focus from ____.
questions.explanation: Education for Sustainable Development calls for learner-centred, action-oriented pedagogy, which moves the focus from teaching to learning.

questions.q: ____ competency is the ability to reflect on one's own role in the local community and (global) society.
questions.explanation: In UNESCO's key sustainability competencies, self-awareness competency means reflecting on one's own role in the local community and global society and evaluating one's own actions.
